overview.description: Gambari-Kan is the three-player variant of Kan from Aomori. One player becomes the lone kankei (solo side) against two mukankei opponents and tries to capture enough point cards in trick play.

history.origins: Gambari-Kan is documented as the three-player branch of the Kan family played in the Tsugaru and Goshogawara area of Aomori.
timeline: Kan family play was established in Aomori before modern online documentation.
Gonin-Kan became the most widespread format, with Gambari-Kan used when only three players are available.
Current published rules describe Gambari-Kan as a one-deal round with rotating dealer and solo-versus-pair structure.
history.evolution: Relative to five-player Kan, Gambari-Kan compresses each round to one deal and uses a kan/pass selection cycle to set the solo side.
history.cultural: It remains part of regional Japanese trick-taking card culture under the broader Kan or Etori umbrella.

setup.players: Exactly three players. One becomes kankei (solo), the other two form mukankei.
setup.deck: 30-card pack: remove all 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s, and 6s, and remove all 7s except the 7 of Spades; include one joker.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and deals 10 cards to each player counterclockwise. No stock remains.

rules.objective: As kankei, take at least the current required number of scoring cards (A, K, Q, J). As mukankei, hold the kankei player below that threshold.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, players in turn from dealer's right may say kan or pass. If all pass, the required scoring-card threshold for kankei is lowered and another pass/kan cycle begins. Once someone declares kan, that player leads and plays alone against the other two. Play is counterclockwise with follow-suit required; if void, any card may be played. Joker and trumps follow Kan-family trick rules, including joker restrictions on first and last trick.
keyRules: Initial requirement for kankei is 9 scoring cards; if all players pass, the requirement is reduced step by step until someone declares kan.
Scoring cards are the A, K, Q, and J of each suit, worth one each.
The kankei player leads the first trick after declaring kan.
Trick play follows Kan conventions: follow suit if possible; joker cannot be led in first or last trick.

strategy.basic: As kankei, declare kan when your hand has control cards and access to likely point tricks rather than waiting too long for a lower threshold.
strategy.intermediate: As mukankei, coordinate by forcing awkward leads and protecting point cards in suits where kankei appears short.
strategy.advanced: Track exposed point cards and timing around joker usage; denying one key trick often flips the whole deal because total scoring cards are limited.
tips: Passing can be strategic: lowering the threshold helps whoever eventually declares kan, so pass only when you expect to seize kan on a later cycle.
Because there is no draw phase, early information from leads and suit follow is highly valuable.

list.name: Clockwise Table Play
list.description: Some groups reverse direction and play clockwise instead of the traditional counterclockwise order.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Clockwise play changes turn order only; engine overrides for direction not yet mapped.

difficulty.easy: Chooses kan too aggressively and misses follow-suit pressure plans as mukankei.
difficulty.medium: Uses threshold and hand texture to decide kan/pass and tracks visible scoring cards.
difficulty.hard: Optimizes kan timing across pass cycles, models suit exhaustion, and preserves joker timing for high-leverage tricks.

considerations: The solo-versus-pair asymmetry requires alliance logic for mukankei and a separate objective policy for kankei.
Kan/pass threshold reduction must be represented explicitly in state transitions.

phases.label: Deal
phases.notes: Deal 10 cards to each of three players.

phases.label: Kan or Pass Selection
phases.notes: Starting at dealer's right, players choose kan or pass. If all pass, lower required scoring-card threshold and repeat.

phases.label: Trick Play
phases.notes: Winner of each trick leads the next trick. Evaluate kankei point-card count at end.

phases.label: Resolve Deal
phases.notes: Apply result based on whether kankei reached required scoring cards.

ante.reason: Gambari-Kan has no ante payment step.

deal.description: Deal ten cards to each of the three players.
deal.constraints: Dealer only at start of the deal.

reveal_market.reason: There is no market reveal system in Gambari-Kan.

buy_market.reason: Cards are never purchased from any market.

buy_stock.reason: No stock-buy action exists in this fixed-deal trick game.

fold.reason: Players remain active through all tricks and cannot fold.

check.reason: There is no betting round where checking applies.

call.reason: No wager matching call action is part of Kan rules.

bet.reason: Gambari-Kan does not use a betting pot.

raise.reason: No betting pot exists, so raising is not applicable.

declare.reason: The core game state uses kan/pass and trick play, not declaration melds.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private during normal play.

award_pot.description: Resolve the deal by checking whether kankei met the required point-card threshold.
award_pot.constraints: System action at end of the ten tricks.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick following suit if possible.
play_card.constraints: Joker cannot be led to first or last trick under standard Kan-family play.

draw.reason: All cards are fully dealt at start; no draw phase exists.

discard.reason: Cards leave hand only through trick play, not a separate discard action.

pass.description: Pass in the kan selection cycle instead of declaring kan.
pass.constraints: Only during kan selection before trick play starts.

bid.description: Declare kan to become the kankei player for the deal.
bid.constraints: Only in pre-play selection; first declaring player becomes kankei.

go_out.reason: The hand ends after fixed trick count, not by a go-out action.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Within trump suit: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in this stripped pack.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Joker cannot be played to first or last trick in standard Kan rules; otherwise normal follow-suit play applies.

edgeCases.text: Each full cycle of passes lowers the required scoring-card threshold before selection repeats.
Joker cannot be played to the first or last trick under standard Kan play.
As in core Kan rules, joker holder cannot be forced to play joker until the late-trick stage.

customLogicNeeded: Implement kan/pass loop with dynamic threshold reduction after each all-pass cycle.
Model solo kankei against two-player mukankei team in scoring and winner resolution.
Apply joker restrictions and late-forced-joker behavior from Kan-family rules.

engine.deckDescription: The deck is a thirty-card stripped pack: all four French suits with ranks Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, and 8, plus the seven of Spades only and one joker, for thirty cards total.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades; the game uses a stripped pack so only certain ranks appear in each suit, with Spades retaining one extra rank (7).
engine.rankDescription: The rank set is Stripped_30: in each suit the ranks are Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, 8, and in Spades only the 7 is also included; one joker is part of the pack and follows Kan-family trick rules.
engine.dealPattern: Counterclockwise, ten cards each to three players.

hero.title: GAMBARI-KAN
hero.subtitle: Solo vs Pair Trick Play
hero.tagline: Declare kan, take point cards, and beat a coordinated two-player defense.

synthesis.shortDescription: Three-player Kan variant where one player declares kan and plays solo against two opponents in a point-trick contest.

prompts.human: Gambari-Kan: decide when to declare kan, then win enough point cards through disciplined trick play.
prompts.ai: Game: Gambari-Kan. Three players. After deal, players may declare kan or pass; declaring player is solo kankei against two mukankei opponents. Play counterclockwise with follow-suit and Kan-family joker restrictions.

scoring.description: In each deal the kankei side must capture at least the current required number of scoring cards (A, K, Q, J). If kankei fails, mukankei wins the deal.
scoring.winCondition: After an agreed session of deals, the highest cumulative score wins.

nullReasons.targetScore: Pagat describes session play by agreed rounds rather than one universal fixed target.
nullReasons.cardValues: Point values for A, K, Q, J are defined in engine.trickConfig.pointValues; scoring.cardValues is not used.

assumptions: Core Kan trick mechanics and joker constraints apply to Gambari-Kan where the source states play is 'as usual'.
